topic: completing short algebraic and segment proofs
subtitle: Justifying each step of an algebraic solution, proving segment relationships with the Segment Addition Postulate, and using the definitions of midpoint and congruent segments

problems.note: Two-column algebraic proof: given 3x + 7 = 25, prove x = 6.

problems.desc: The Reasons column of the two-column proof - Subtraction Property of Equality then Division Property of Equality. A written justification, read by a teacher.

problems.note: Segment Addition Postulate: AB + BC = AC with AB = 2x+5, BC = x+3, AC = 26 cm.

problems.desc: Naming the Segment Addition Postulate as the statement that licenses AB + BC = AC. A written justification, read by a teacher.

problems.note: Two-column algebraic proof: given 5(x - 2) = 3x + 8, prove x = 9.

problems.desc: The missing Statements and Reasons of the two-column proof - Distributive Property, Subtraction Property of Equality, Addition Property of Equality, Division Property of Equality. A written justification, read by a teacher.

problems.note: M is the midpoint of AB, AM = 4x - 1, MB = 2x + 7 cm.

problems.desc: The Reasons column - definition of midpoint, then the definition of congruent segments, then the properties of equality used to solve. A written justification, read by a teacher.

problems.note: A, B, C, D collinear in that order: AB + BC + CD = AD with AD = 37 cm.
Congruent segments: AB = 3x + 4 and CD = 5x - 12 with AB congruent to CD.

problems.desc: The Reasons column - definition of congruent segments, Subtraction Property of Equality, Addition Property of Equality, Division Property of Equality, then Substitution. A written justification, read by a teacher.

problems.note: Error analysis: a flawed proof of 2(x + 3) = 4x - 10 subtracts 2x from one side only.

problems.desc: Identifying which line of the flawed proof is wrong and naming the property it misuses - the Subtraction Property of Equality requires subtracting from both sides. A written justification, read by a teacher.

problems.note: A, B, C, D collinear in that order with AB = 2x - 3 and CD = x + 5 congruent.

problems.desc: The general two-column proof that AB congruent to CD forces AC congruent to BD for four collinear points - Segment Addition Postulate, Addition Property of Equality, Substitution. A written proof, read by a teacher.
